questions.q: A BI tool connects via a standard SQL connection string and issues T-SQL queries with joins and window functions, requiring strict schema. Which Fabric item fits?
questions.explain: A Warehouse (Fabric Lesson 10) provides the full T-SQL surface with enforced schema, unlike a Lakehouse's read-only SQL endpoint subset.

questions.q: Which Fabric item's SQL endpoint supports INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements?
questions.explain: A Lakehouse's SQL endpoint is read-only; writes to a Lakehouse happen via Spark, a pipeline, or a Dataflow, never the SQL endpoint directly.

questions.q: How does a Warehouse's transactional behavior compare to a Lakehouse's?
options: They are functionally identical in every transactional respect
A Warehouse supports full multi-table ACID transactions with rollback; a Lakehouse relies on Delta Lake's per-table ACID guarantees instead
A Lakehouse supports multi-table transactions but a Warehouse does not
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 11 draws this distinction directly: Warehouse transactions match traditional SQL Server behavior, while Lakehouse consistency comes from Delta Lake (Databricks Lesson 18).

questions.q: A scenario says a team needs to run a stored procedure with multiple UPDATE statements inside a single transaction that must fully roll back on failure. What Fabric item is required?
questions.explain: Multi-statement transactional rollback requires the Warehouse's full T-SQL transaction support; a Lakehouse doesn't offer this at the multi-table level.

questions.q: What is the main reason a Lakehouse's SQL endpoint is described as 'read-only'?
options: Lakehouses cannot be queried with SQL at all
Read-only is a misnomer and Lakehouses fully support SQL writes
Lakehouse data is stored in a format SQL cannot read
Writes to Lakehouse tables happen through Spark, pipelines, or Dataflows, not through direct SQL statements against the endpoint
questions.explain: This read/write asymmetry between Warehouse and Lakehouse SQL endpoints is one of the most exam-tested Domain 1 facts.

questions.q: Why would a team choose a Warehouse over a Lakehouse specifically for a finance reporting workload?
options: Warehouses are always cheaper regardless of workload
Warehouses support Spark notebooks better than Lakehouses
The workload needs strict schema enforcement and full T-SQL, including writes, which only a Warehouse's SQL endpoint provides
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 11's Lakehouse-vs-Warehouse guidance: strict-schema, SQL-write-heavy workloads point to Warehouse.
